mainTopic: ברכות on lettuce as מרור, הלל's wrapping of מצה and מרור (the source of כורך), and washing hands for dipped foods
overview: This amud opens with רב חסדא challenging רב הונא's order of ברכות when lettuce is eaten twice at the סדר. רב חסדא says both בורא פרי האדמה and על אכילת מרור are said at the first eating, and the הלכה follows him. רב אחא בריה דרבא avoided the dispute by using a different vegetable first. Next, a tradition in the name of a sage called הלל says not to wrap מצה and מרור together nowadays, because the rabbinic מרור would cancel the Torah-level מצה. The גמרא then shows that הלל הזקן did wrap them together, based on the פסוק. רבי יוחנן says הלל's colleagues disagreed, but רב אשי rereads their ברייתא: it only says wrapping is not required. Since no ruling was made, we eat מצה and מרור separately with ברכות, then together as a זכר למקדש. The amud ends with a new rule that food dipped in liquid requires נטילת ידים, and רב פפא begins applying it to the lettuce, a thought that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב חסדא objects to blessing after eating
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא attacks רב הונא's order. After eating lettuce at the first dipping, how can you later say a מצוה-ברכה on that same lettuce?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא objects: After he has already filled his stomach with it, he goes back and makes a blessing on it?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא challenges רב הונא's ruling. Under that ruling, the ברכה of על אכילת מרור is said only at the second eating of lettuce, after the person already ate it at the first dipping.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא had said: at the first dipping, say only בורא פרי האדמה, and later say על אכילת מרור. רב חסדא argues this is backwards. The person already ate plenty of this very vegetable, so saying its מצוה-ברכה afterward looks odd. The ברכה should come before you first eat it, not after you have already filled up on it.

keyTerms.meaning: He strongly objects to it (introduces a challenge)
Goes back and recites a blessing

phrases.english: Rav Chisda objects to it:
after he has filled his belly from it
phrases.notes: This is the lettuce he already ate at the first dipping.

phrases.english: he goes back and recites a blessing over it?
phrases.notes: He's not really asking here; it's a challenge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's ruling from the previous section of the daf
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that על אכילת מרור is said only at the later eating of lettuce
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A מצוה-ברכה belongs before the first real eating. Saying it after you already ate your fill of the same vegetable makes no sense.

steps.title: רב חסדא's order: both blessings at the start
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that both בורא פרי האדמה and על אכילת מרור are said at the first eating of the lettuce. The later eating has no ברכה at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב חסדא said: At the start he says over it both בורא פרי האדמה and על אכילת מרור, and eats it. At the end, he eats the lettuce without any ברכה.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected רב הונא's order, רב חסדא gives his own: say both ברכות at the very first eating of the lettuce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב חסדא, the first eating of lettuce already counts as the מצוה of מרור. So both the food-ברכה and the מצוה-ברכה belong there. The second eating, later in the סדר, is just a repeat and gets no ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: The blessing over vegetables: 'Who creates fruit of the ground'

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Chisda said:
At the start he blesses over it
"Who creates fruit of the ground"
and "on eating maror," and eats,
and at the end he eats an eating of lettuce
without a blessing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב הונא's order with a new one after the challenge
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both ברכות are said at the first eating of lettuce. The later eating has no ברכה.

steps.title: How different communities practiced
steps.stepSummary: In סוריא they followed רב הונא, while רב ששת בריה דרב יהושע followed רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: In Syria they act like רב הונא, and רב ששת בריה דרב יהושע acted like רב חסדא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports real-life practice: which places and people followed each view. This sets up the final ruling in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before giving the final הלכה, the גמרא shows that both opinions were actually followed. So this was a live dispute in practice, not just a theory.

phrases.english: In Syria they act like Rav Huna,
and Rav Sheshet son of Rav Yehoshua
acted like Rav Chisda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports how the רב הונא / רב חסדא dispute was practiced
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סוריא followed רב הונא. רב ששת בריה דרב יהושע followed רב חסדא.

steps.title: The halacha follows רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that the הלכה follows רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is like רב חסדא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling on the dispute: follow רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In practice, when lettuce is used for both dippings, both ברכות are said at the first eating. The second eating has no ברכה.

keyTerms.meaning: The halacha is in accordance with him

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows רב חסדא: when the same vegetable serves as both the first dip and the מרור, say בורא פרי האדמה and על אכילת מרור at the first eating.

phrases.english: And the halacha is in accordance with Rav Chisda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between the two practices just reported

steps.title: רב אחא avoids the dispute with other vegetables
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא would look for a different vegetable for the first dipping. That way he was not caught in the dispute at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רבא would search for other vegetables, to take himself out of the dispute.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells how one אמורא avoided the whole question by using a different vegetable for the first dipping.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dispute only arises when the same lettuce is used twice. With a different vegetable first, he says בורא פרי האדמה on it. Then he says על אכילת מרור on the lettuce later. Every opinion is satisfied.

keyTerms.meaning: To remove himself from the dispute

phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rava
would seek out other vegetables
to take himself out of the dispute.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא מְהַדַּר אַשְּׁאָר יְרָקוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows a practical way to avoid the dispute just ruled on
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a source for using a different vegetable (כרפס) for the first dipping, so the ברכה question never comes up.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Using a different vegetable for the first dipping avoids the dispute entirely.

steps.title: Do not wrap מצה and מרור together nowadays
steps.stepSummary: רבינא reports a tradition in הלל's name: do not wrap מצה and מרור together nowadays. The rabbinic מרור would cancel the Torah-level מצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: רב משרשיא בריה דרב נתן told me that הלל said this, citing tradition: A person should not wrap מצה and מרור together and eat them. This is because we hold that nowadays מצה is a Torah obligation, while מרור is only rabbinic. The rabbinic מרור would come and cancel the Torah מצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: is it okay to eat מצה and מרור wrapped together? This tradition says no.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the קרבן פסח, the Torah obligation of מרור no longer applies, so מרור today is only דרבנן. מצה remains דאורייתא even today. If the two are eaten together, the taste of the rabbinic מרור 'cancels' the Torah-level eating of מצה, and you lose your Torah מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of received tradition

steps.confusionAlert: The הלל quoted here, who says not to wrap, cannot be הלל הזקן. Step 9 shows that הלל הזקן did wrap מצה and מרור together, so רשב"ם explains that this is a later sage with the same name. This is also not the final word on wrapping. Step 13 concludes that we also eat them together, without a ברכה, as a זכר למקדש like הלל. That is the source of our כורך.

phrases.english: Ravina said:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לִי רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נָתָן,
phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiya son of Rav Natan told me,
thus said Hillel, in the name of tradition:
A person should not wrap
matzah and maror together and eat them,
because we hold
that matzah nowadays is a Torah obligation,
and maror is rabbinic,
and the rabbinic maror comes
and nullifies the Torah-level matzah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא: אָמַר לִי רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: wrapping מצה and מרור together
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not wrap מצה and מרור together nowadays, because the rabbinic מרור would cancel the Torah מצה.

steps.title: Why 'מצוות do not cancel each other' does not help here
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא heads off a question. Even the view that מצות אין מבטלות זו את זו only means that when both are the same level. A rabbinic מצוה does cancel a Torah one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even according to the one who says that מצוות do not cancel each other out, that applies only to Torah with Torah, or rabbinic with rabbinic. But when one is Torah and the other is rabbinic, the rabbinic one comes and cancels the Torah one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an expected objection: 'But aren't there views that מצוות never cancel each other?' It limits that principle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The principle מצות אין מבטלות זו את זו applies only between two מצוות of equal level: both דאורייתא or both דרבנן. When one is דאורייתא and the other is דרבנן, the weaker rabbinic one can still swamp the Torah one. So the ruling of the previous step holds according to everyone.

keyTerms.term: מִצְוֹת אֵין מְבַטְּלוֹת זוֹ אֶת זוֹ
keyTerms.meaning: מצוות do not nullify one another
These words apply (only) to... (a limiting formula)
According to the one who says

steps.whatToRemember: Nowadays מצה is דאורייתא and מרור is דרבנן. Mixing levels allows the rabbinic מצוה to cancel the Torah one, even for those who hold מצות אין מבטלות זו את זו.

phrases.english: And even according to the one who says:

phrases.aramaic: מִצְוֹת אֵין מְבַטְּלוֹת זוֹ אֶת זוֹ,
phrases.english: מצוות do not nullify one another,
that applies only to Torah with Torah
or rabbinic with rabbinic,
but Torah and rabbinic —
the rabbinic one comes and nullifies the Torah one.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ לְמַאן דְּאָמַר: מִצְוֹת אֵין מְבַטְּלוֹת זוֹ אֶת זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends step 6 against an expected objection
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a principle
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think that those who hold מצות אין מבטלות זו את זו would allow wrapping מצה and מרור together.
steps.terutzMaskana: That principle only covers מצוות of equal level. A דרבנן מצוה can cancel a דאורייתא one, so wrapping is still a problem.

steps.title: Who holds that מצוות do not cancel each other?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא is the source for the view that מצות אין מבטלות זו את זו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the תנא you heard say that מצות do not cancel each other?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It asks who is behind the view it just mentioned in Step 7, that מצות do not cancel each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 mentioned this view without naming anyone. Now the גמרא wants to know who holds it, so it can see what that person actually did in practice.

keyTerms.term: מִצְוֹת אֵין מְבַטְּלוֹת זוֹ אֶת זוֹ
keyTerms.meaning: מצוות do not cancel each other out

phrases.english: Who is the tanna that you heard say

phrases.aramaic: מִצְוֹת אֵין מְבַטְּלוֹת זוֹ אֶת זוֹ?
phrases.english: that מצוות do not cancel each other?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks who holds the view that Step 7 referred to
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the תנא who holds מצות אין מבטלות זו את זו

steps.title: It is הלל, who wrapped מצה and מרור together
steps.stepSummary: The view belongs to הלל. A ברייתא reports that he wrapped מצה and מרור together and ate them, based on the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is הלל. A ברייתא teaches: they said about הלל that he would wrap them together and eat them, as it says, "With מצות and bitter herbs they shall eat it."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the view is הלל's. It proves this from a ברייתא describing how he ate מצה and מרור wrapped together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If eating the two together made one מצוה cancel the other, הלל would not have done it. So his practice shows that he holds מצות do not cancel each other. He reads the פסוק as telling us to eat them together.

keyTerms.meaning: He wraps them (the מצה and מרור) together
"With מצות and bitter herbs they shall eat it" (במדבר ט:יא)

phrases.english: It is Hillel.
As it was taught in a baraita: they said about Hillel
that he would wrap them together and eat them,
as it says: "With matzos and bitter herbs they shall eat it."

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הלל holds that מצות do not cancel each other, as shown by his practice of wrapping מצה and מרור together

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says הלל's colleagues disagree
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says הלל's colleagues argue with him. He brings a ברייתא that reads the same פסוק as allowing each food to be eaten on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: הלל's colleagues disagree with him. A ברייתא teaches: You might think one should wrap them together and eat them the way הלל ate them. So the פסוק says, "With מצות and bitter herbs they shall eat it," meaning even this one by itself and that one by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן brings a ברייתא to show that the other חכמים argue with הלל. In their view, the פסוק allows eating מצה and מרור separately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן reads the ברייתא as rejecting הלל's wrapping. That would mean הלל's colleagues hold that מצות do cancel each other. The same פסוק is read in opposite directions.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
His colleagues disagree with Hillel.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: יָכוֹל יְהֵא כּוֹרְכָן בְּבַת אַחַת
phrases.english: As it was taught: You might think one should wrap them together
and eat them the way Hillel ate them;
therefore the verse says: "With matzos and bitter herbs they shall eat it,"

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ זֶה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ וְזֶה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ.
phrases.english: even this by itself and that by itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: חוֹלְקִין עָלָיו חֲבֵירָיו עַל הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds that הלל's view is disputed
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הלל's colleagues disagree with him and do not wrap מצה and מרור together

steps.title: רב אשי asks: what does "even" mean?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי objects to רבי יוחנן's reading. If the ברייתא rejects wrapping, why does it use the word "even"?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי objected: If so, what is the meaning of "even"?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי challenges רבי יוחנן's reading of the ברייתא. He points to a single word, "even" (אפילו).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "even" means separate eating is also allowed, on top of something else. That suggests wrapping is still fine. So the ברייתא does not seem to reject הלל's way at all.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the point of the word "even"?

phrases.english: Rav Ashi objected to it:
If so, what is the meaning of "even"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אָשֵׁי: אִי הָכִי, מַאי אֲפִילּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יוחנן's reading of the ברייתא
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that the ברייתא rejects הלל's practice
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word "even" shows that separate eating is an added option, not a replacement. So wrapping is not being rejected.

steps.title: רב אשי rereads the ברייתא: wrapping is not required
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that the ברייתא only teaches that one is not required to wrap. Eating each food separately also works.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: This תנא is teaching this: You might think one only fulfills his obligation if he wraps them together and eats them the way הלל did. So the פסוק says, "With מצות and bitter herbs they shall eat it," meaning even this one by itself and that one by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a new reading of the ברייתא. It does not argue against wrapping. It only says wrapping is not a must.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי יוחנן's reading, the colleagues forbid wrapping. Under רב אשי's reading, they allow both ways. The only point they reject is הלל's claim that wrapping is required.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he is teaching

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two readings. רבי יוחנן reads the ברייתא as saying wrapping is not good. רב אשי reads it as saying wrapping is not required.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
This tanna is teaching as follows:

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל לֹא יָצָא בְּהוּ יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ
phrases.english: You might think one does not fulfill his obligation with them

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן כּוֹרְכָן בְּבַת אַחַת וְאוֹכְלָן
phrases.english: unless he wraps them together and eats them
the way Hillel ate them;
therefore the verse says: "With matzos and bitter herbs they shall eat it":

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ זֶה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ וְזֶה בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ.
phrases.english: even this by itself and that by itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי, הַאי תַּנָּא הָכִי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves רב אשי's own question by rereading the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא rejects הלל's wrapping, so the colleagues hold that מצות cancel each other
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא only denies that wrapping is required. Eating separately is also valid.

steps.title: Practical procedure: separately with ברכות, then together as a זכר למקדש
steps.stepSummary: Since the הלכה was not decided, we eat מצה with its ברכה, then מרור with its ברכה. Then we eat מצה and חסא together without a ברכה, as a זכר למקדש in the way of הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that the הלכה was not stated like הלל or like the רבנן, one says the ברכה "על אכילת מצה" and eats. Then he says "על אכילת מרור" and eats. Then he eats מצה and lettuce together without a ברכה, as a זכר למקדש, like הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the practical bottom line for the סדר night. Because no final ruling was made, we cover both views.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating each food on its own with its own ברכה fulfills the מצוה according to the רבנן. It also avoids the problem from Steps 6-7 of the rabbinic מרור cancelling the Torah מצה. Then we eat them wrapped together, with no ברכה, to remember how הלל ate them in the times of the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that no ruling was stated
A remembrance of the בית המקדש

steps.whatToRemember: At the סדר: מצה alone with a ברכה, then מרור alone with a ברכה, then כורך (both together) without a ברכה as a זכר למקדש, like הלל.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the כורך step in the הגדה that we do every פסח.

phrases.english: Now that the halacha was not stated
neither like Hillel nor like the Rabbis,
one blesses "on eating matza" and eats,
and then blesses "on eating maror" and eats,

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲדַר אָכֵיל מַצָּה וְחַסָּא בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי
phrases.english: and then eats matza and lettuce together
without a blessing, in remembrance of the Temple, like Hillel.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא דְּלָא אִיתְּמַר הִלְכְתָא לָא כְּהִלֵּל וְלָא כְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the unresolved dispute into a practical procedure that satisfies both views
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Eat מצה and מרור separately, each with its own ברכה, then eat them together without a ברכה as a זכר למקדש like הלל

steps.title: Food dipped in liquid requires washing the hands
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר quotes רב אושעיא: any food that is dipped in a liquid requires נטילת ידים before it is eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said in the name of רב אושעיא: Anything that is dipped in a liquid requires washing of the hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule. If you eat food that has been dipped into a liquid, you must wash your hands first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים treat unwashed hands as having a low level of טומאה (שני לטומאה). That level cannot make ordinary food טמא directly, but it does make any liquid the hands touch טמא at a stronger level. That liquid can then pass טומאה on to the food dipped in it. That is why a food dipped in liquid requires נטילת ידים even when one is not eating bread.

keyTerms.meaning: Dipping a food into a liquid before eating it
A liquid, such as water, wine, or vinegar
The ritual washing of the hands before eating

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the usual washing before bread. It is a separate rule for any food that is dipped in a liquid, even a vegetable.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule explains why some people wash their hands at the סדר before eating the כרפס, which is dipped in salt water.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said
Rav Oshaya said:
phrases.notes: רבי אלעזר is quoting his teacher's teaching.

phrases.english: Anything that is dipped in a liquid —
requires washing of the hands.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from how to eat מצה and מרור to a new rule about washing the hands before eating dipped foods.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any food dipped in a liquid requires נטילת ידים before eating.

steps.title: רב פפא begins drawing a lesson about the lettuce
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא starts to draw a practical conclusion from רב אושעיא's rule about the lettuce (חסא) used on פסח. His statement continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Learn from this that this lettuce...
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא begins to take a lesson from the rule just taught and apply it to the lettuce eaten at the סדר. This is a setup line, and the rest of his conclusion comes in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase שמע מינה means that a new practical rule is being taken from an earlier one. Since dipping in a liquid brings in the need to wash, רב פפא is about to explain what this means for the חסא, which is dipped in חרוסת at the סדר.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this. It is used to draw a conclusion from what was just said.
Lettuce, the preferred vegetable for מרור

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence breaks off in the middle. Do not try to guess the full rule yet. The ending of רב פפא's statement comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Learn from this: this lettuce
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes רב אושעיא's general rule and starts to apply it to the חסא of the סדר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Incomplete on this amud. רב פפא begins to draw a rule about the חסא from the washing requirement for dipped foods.
